title: 21 Southern Tier Attorneys Honored in Best Lawyers 2026 - NewsBreak
text:
By Traci Taylor ,
2 hours ago
It’s not every day that our little corner of New York makes national headlines, but this week it sure did. Coughlin & Gerhart, LLP, a law firm many in the Southern Tier already know, just had 21 of its attorneys recognized in the 2026 editions of The Best Lawyers in America and Best Lawyers: Ones to Watch.
How Best Lawyers Chooses the Best of the Best If you’re not familiar, Best Lawyers is kind of like the Oscars of the legal world . Lawyers don’t buy their way onto the list. Instead, it’s all based on confidential peer reviews, other attorneys around the country saying, “Yes, this person is one of the best at what they do.” Only a small percentage ever make it, which makes this achievement even bigger.
Meet the Local Attorneys Making National Waves Among the honorees are people you may have already seen working hard in our community . Managing Partner Rachel Abbott was recognized for her work in personal injury cases. Mark Gorgos made the list for education law. Robert Jones earned honors for both trusts and estates litigation and personal injury. And Carrie Wenban, who practices corporate and business law in Ithaca, also took home national recognition.
READ MORE: Heartbreak in Broome County: Toddler Dies in Fire, GoFundMe Launched
All told, 16 attorneys from the firm were listed in Best Lawyers . On top of that, five more up and coming attorneys were highlighted in Ones to Watch, a category for rising stars who are already making their mark in areas like family law, real estate, municipal law, and elder law.
Why These Honors Matter Beyond the Awards For the rest of us in the Southern Tier, this isn’t just about awards and recognition. It means that when life throws tough legal situations our way, whether it’s a family matter, a business issue, or something as personal as an injury, there are trusted, nationally recognized experts right here at home.
World-Class Representation, Right Here in the Southern Tier Rachel Abbott, the firm’s managing partner, summed it up best: these honors aren’t just about skill, they’re about integrity, professionalism, and serving clients well. And really, that’s what makes this news worth celebrating.
Download the WHWK Mobile App Now So if you’ve ever wondered whether world class legal representation exists in the Southern Tier, the answer is a resounding yes and now the rest of the country knows it too.
Five Things Banned or Illegal in New York These are five things that New York has either banned or made illegal in the state in the last five years. Gallery Credit: Traci Taylor Canva New York Polystyrene (Styrofoam) Ban In 2020, New York banned packing peanuts, single-use Styrofoam food and beverage containers, and packing peanuts. Canva New York Plastic Bag Ban In 2020, New York banned single-use plastic bags like the ones groceries were put in at supermarkets. Then, the pandemic hit, and bags were allowed to be used again. Now, things have tightened back up again and stores are no longer allowed to offer plastic bags in New York. Joe Raedle / Getty Images New York Laundry Detergent Ban New York says that some laundry detergent brands contain high levels of potentially cancer-causing chemicals. So, the New York State Department of Conservation has placed a legal limit on the amount of these chemicals that can be found in laundry detergent. Unless manufacturers can bring the chemical amount down, the laundry detergent will be banned from sale in New York. Canva New York Gas Powered Vehicles Ban - Kind Of In September of 2021, Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation that bans the sale of new, internal combustion engine cars and trucks by 2035. In other words, gas-powered vehicles. Canva New York Pesticide Ban In April of 2022, New York made it illegal for any pesticides to be used at any camp which operates as a camp for children. Six Vehicle Modifications That Are Illegal in New York If you live in New York, before you make any modifications to your vehicle, you might want to check out the six modifications that are illegal in the state. Gallery Credit: Traci Taylor Canva Vehicle Frame and Suspension Believe it or not, there are no regulations in New York when it comes to suspension and frame lift height. However, all cars and SUVs are required to have bumpers mounted between 16 and 20 inches. In New York, trucks have a maximum bumper height of 30 inches. Canva Vehicle Sound System Love a good thump? That's cool but just don't go overboard in New York because here, sound that is 15 or more decibels above the ambient sound in a given area when measured 15 or more feet from the source is not allowed. Canva Vehicle Window Tint Non-reflective tint is allowed but only on the top six inches of the windshield. Rear windows can have any tint darkness but your front, back, and side windows are required to allow in over 70 percent of light. If your back window is tinted, side mirrors are absolutely required. Canva Vehicle Mufflers Loud muffler? You can definitely get pulled over if its sound level is higher than 15 decibels more than the ambient sound of the vehicle being driven. On that note, muffler cutouts are illegal in New York. Canva Vehicle Lights If you drive an emergency vehicle, you can have red and blue flashing lights on it. If you do not drive an emergency vehicke, you cannot. Also, the only vehicle lights allowed are ones installed at the factory which means you cannot have auxiliary lights on your vehicle. Canva Vehicle Engines New York doesn't have any regulations on engine swaps or modifications but keep in mind that any vehicle registered in New York is required to undergo testing and safety inspections every year.
